issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s statements deny the landlord’s title for eviction purposes only when the denial is clear and unequivocal.
material_facts: The tenant had been inducted by the original owner and, after a dispute over ownership was resolved in the landlord’s favour, recognised the landlord and paid rent.

The tenant later sued only the municipal authorities after receiving a notice requiring removal of the premises as allegedly built on government land; the suit challenged the notice and sought protection against interference with possession.
The landlord was not a target of the earlier suit, and the tenant sought no relief against the landlord in it.
The tenant described his possession as that of a tenant and did not claim title to the premises for himself.
The statements in the earlier plaint, read as a whole and in context, did not clearly and unambiguously deny the landlord’s title.
issues.conclusion: The tenant had not denied the landlord’s title in clear and unequivocal terms, so eviction on that ground was not established. The Court allowed the appeal, set aside the judgments below, and dismissed the eviction suit.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13(1)(f) of the Rajasthan Premises (Control of Rent and Eviction) Act, 1950 gives effect to section 111(g) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882. The forfeiture principle rests on the rule that a person cannot approbate and reprobate; because forfeiture has serious consequences, denial of the landlord’s title must be clear and unequivocal. The Court relied on Mohammad Amir Ahmad Khan v. Municipal Board of Sitapur, AIR 1965 SC 1923.

rule.if: tenant_eviction_proceeding and prior_suit_aimed_only_at_authority and tenant_described_possession_as_tenancy and not tenant_claimed_own_title and not denial_clear_and_unequivocal

predicates.tenant_eviction_proceeding: A landlord seeks to evict a tenant on the basis that the tenant denied the landlord’s title.
predicates.prior_suit_aimed_only_at_authority: The tenant’s earlier suit challenging action affecting the premises was directed only against a public authority, not the landlord.
predicates.tenant_described_possession_as_tenancy: In the earlier suit, the tenant described the character of the tenant’s possession as a tenancy.
predicates.tenant_claimed_own_title: The tenant claimed ownership of the premises for himself.
predicates.denial_clear_and_unequivocal: The tenant made a clear and unambiguous denial of the landlord’s title.

issues.definition: When an eviction proceeding based on denial of title concerns statements made in an earlier suit directed only at a public authority, and the tenant described possession as a tenancy without claiming ownership, the absence of a clear and unequivocal denial means eviction on that ground is not permitted.
